title: @origingame/engine API v1
description:
The Origin Engine API. Game code declares components and systems, and reads the world through typed views over engine memory.
Every failure is a returned Result; desc objects may omit any field; nothing reads the wall clock inside a tick.

x-og-units.cssPx: CSS pixels of the play surface, origin at the top left
x-og-units.perSecond: a rate per second: the fraction of a value that decays in one second
x-og-units.kgPerM3: kilograms per cubic metre (per square metre in the 2D profile)

x-og-modules.name: math
x-og-modules.doc: Plain math values in the three.js vocabulary. They are data: the engine owns the operations, so results are identical on every host.

x-og-modules.name: reflect
x-og-modules.doc:
Reflection: components and resources are declared once with their field layout and metadata, and registered by name.
The inspector, Tune, the probe, scene text and the wiki read this one schema. Each column factory below makes one field.

functions.name: defineComponent
functions.doc:
Declare a component: plain data stored per entity in engine memory, one column per field.
Registration is by name, so a hot reload re-registers the same component and migrates its fields by name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The component's unique name, PascalCase, as it appears in scenes and dumps.

params.name: fields
params.doc: The layout: field names to column factories, as `{ hp: f32(100) }`.

functions.returnsDoc: The token systems, queries and the world take.

functions.name: defineResource
functions.doc: Declare a resource: a reflected singleton, such as a tuning table. Its fields start at their defaults.
functions.returnsDoc: The token `world.resource` and system declarations take.

x-og-modules.name: world
x-og-modules.doc:
The world: an archetype ECS. Entities are generational handles; components are columns in engine memory.
Structural changes (spawn, despawn, insert, remove) invalidate typed views; the API refuses a stale view.

interfaces.name: World
interfaces.doc: The world a system, a command or a game callback is handed. Game code never holds a world beyond the call it was passed to.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps taken since the world was created.

members.name: spawn
members.doc: Spawn an entity.
members.returnsDoc: The new entity, or why it was refused (a duplicate name, a dead parent).

members.name: despawn
members.doc: Despawn an entity and its descendants.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity.

members.name: alive
members.doc: Whether an entity handle is live.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether an entity has a component.

members.name: insert
members.doc: Add a component to an entity, or overwrite it when present. A structural change.

params.name: value
params.doc: Field values; omitted fields take their defaults.

members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or an unregistered component.

members.name: remove
members.doc: Remove a component from an entity. A structural change.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: get
members.doc: Copy one entity's component value. For bulk work use a system's typed views.

members.name: set
members.doc: Write some fields of one entity's component.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead entity or a component it does not have.

members.name: resource
members.doc: A resource's live value. Inside a system, the resource must be among the system's reads or writes.
members.returnsDoc: Refused for an unregistered resource or one the running system did not declare.

members.name: find
members.doc: The entity with a name.
members.returnsDoc: Null when no live entity has the name.

members.name: nameOf
members.doc: An entity's name.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unnamed or dead entity.

members.name: query
members.doc: A query over the current archetypes, for commands and callbacks; systems receive theirs.

members.name: events
members.doc: The events of one type emitted during the previous tick and this one, oldest first.

members.name: emit
members.doc: Emit an event; readers see it this tick and the next.

members.name: instantiate
members.doc:
Spawn a loaded scene or glTF asset into the world: a root entity from the desc, then (for a scene) every scene entity under it with its components and names, or (for a glTF) a Model on the root.
Scene entity names must be free: a name already in use refuses the whole instantiation before anything spawns.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Name, parent and transform of the root entity.

members.returnsDoc: The root entity, or why it was refused (an asset still loading, a failed asset).

interfaces.name: Query
interfaces.doc: A set of matched archetypes. Iterate archetypes, never entities one by one.

members.name: archetypes
members.doc: The matched archetypes this tick.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of matched entities.

interfaces.name: ArchetypeView
interfaces.doc: One archetype's columns for this tick. Views are invalidated by structural changes; using a stale view throws with the tick and the system it belonged to.

members.name: count
members.doc: The number of entities in the archetype.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The tick this view belongs to.

members.name: entities
members.doc: The entities as (index, generation) pairs: entity i is at 2i and 2i + 1.

members.name: entity
members.doc: The handle of entity i.

members.name: has
members.doc: Whether the archetype carries a component.

members.name: column
members.doc:
The typed views of a component's fields: one typed array per field, `count * stride` long.
Writing requires the component among the system's writes; reading among its reads or writes.

x-og-modules.name: system
x-og-modules.doc:
Systems: functions the engine calls once per tick with their matched archetypes.
A system declares what it reads and writes; a write to an undeclared component is refused at registration with the field name.

functions.name: defineSystem
functions.doc: Declare a system.

members.name: name
members.doc: The system's unique name.

members.name: reads
members.doc: What it reads.

members.name: writes
members.doc: What it writes.

callbacks.name: SystemRun
callbacks.doc: A system's body. It is called once per tick; loop over `q.archetypes()`, then over rows.

params.name: q
params.doc: The archetypes matching the declared components.

params.name: time
params.doc: The Time resource for this tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world, for resources, events and structural changes.

x-og-modules.name: game
x-og-modules.doc: The game entry: what the bundle's default export declares.

functions.name: game
functions.doc: Declare the game. The bundle's default export is its result.

interfaces.name: Game
interfaces.doc: A declared game, the bundle's default export.

members.name: tick
members.doc: The fixed tick rate in hertz.

members.name: systems
members.doc: The systems in declaration order.

callbacks.name: FactsFn
callbacks.doc: The game's own facts for the probe's state(): a small JSON object, computed from the world without changing it.

callbacks.name: StartFn
callbacks.doc: The game's setup: called once before the first tick, after GameDesc.scene has spawned. Spawn, insert, load and set resources here; systems then only read and write their views.

x-og-modules.name: transform
x-og-modules.doc: Transforms in the three.js vocabulary: position, quaternion and scale, composed into matrixWorld down the parent chain.

functions.name: compose
functions.doc: A matrix from position, rotation and scale, as three.js Matrix4.compose.

functions.name: decompose
functions.doc: Position, rotation and scale from a matrix, as three.js Matrix4.decompose.

functions.name: lookAt
functions.doc: The rotation that points -Z from an eye towards a target, as three.js Object3D.lookAt for cameras.

params.name: up
params.doc: The up direction; the zero vector means +Y.

functions.name: fromAxisAngle
functions.doc: A rotation about an axis, as three.js Quaternion.setFromAxisAngle.

x-og-modules.name: time
x-og-modules.doc: Simulation time. Game code never reads the wall clock; it reads Time.

x-og-modules.name: rng
x-og-modules.doc: Deterministic randomness. Every random draw comes from an Rng stream; the sequence for a seed is identical on every host and in the Web scaffold's rng.ts.

interfaces.name: RngStream
interfaces.doc: One generator stream, forked from the Rng resource for a subsystem that must not perturb the main sequence.

members.name: seed
members.doc: The stream's derived seed.

members.name: next
members.doc: Uniform in [0, 1).

members.name: range
members.doc: Uniform in [low, high).

members.name: integer
members.doc: A uniform integer in [low, high].

members.name: chance
members.doc: True with probability p.

members.name: fork
members.doc: A fresh stream on a seed derived from this stream's seed and a label.

params.name: label
params.doc: The subsystem's name; the same label always gives the same stream.

x-og-modules.name: input
x-og-modules.doc:
Input as the game sees it: the Input resource for polling, events for edges.
The shell collects pointer, keyboard and wheel input on the main thread; the probe and the command channel inject through the same path.

x-og-modules.name: camera
x-og-modules.doc:
The main camera, as a resource with three.js PerspectiveCamera and OrthographicCamera parameter names.
Camera controllers are components (OrbitCamera, FollowCamera, Follow2D) on the entity the camera orbits or follows; the systems that drive them ship in TypeScript as og.systems.cameras.

x-og-modules.name: render
x-og-modules.doc: What is drawn: meshes with materials. Draws are instanced by (geometry, material) automatically; there is no per-object draw call.

consts.name: MAX_LIGHTS
consts.doc: The most point and spot lights one frame draws.

functions.name: sprite
functions.doc: Draw a sprite this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit it every tick the sprite should show.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The texture, placement, region and colour.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead texture.

functions.name: measureText
functions.doc: The size text takes when og.render.text draws it, for centring, wrapping and layout.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: boxGeometry
functions.doc: Make a box geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a convex or triangle-mesh Collider.mesh too.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: planeGeometry
functions.doc: Make a plane geometry for og.Mesh. Physics can use it as a triangle-mesh Collider.mesh too.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: sphereGeometry
functions.doc: Make a sphere geometry for og.Mesh (give its body a sphere Collider, not this mesh).

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the geometry.

functions.name: standardMaterial
functions.doc: Create a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters; omitted ones take three.js defaults.

functions.name: updateMaterial
functions.doc: Change some parameters of a standard material.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the material.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameters to change; omitted ones keep their values.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead material.

functions.name: capabilities
functions.doc: The renderer's tier and limits on this device.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer is asked.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: Draw text this frame. Systems and commands may call it; the list is cleared at every tick, so submit it every tick the text should show. Multi-page fonts are drawn page by page with one layout.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer draws it.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The font, text, placement and colour.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

x-og-modules.name: load
x-og-modules.doc:
Asset loading from cooked output: `og cook` turns assets/ into cooked/ (.ogb blobs and the manifest cooked/.cook.ogt), and the runtime reads only cooked/.
Paths are asset ids: the path under assets/ (`models/ship.glb`, `scenes/main.ogt`); an `assets/` prefix is accepted. Every blob is checked against the manifest's type, schema version and cook stamp.
The game's bundle (`cooked`) is opened before the first tick and GameDesc.scene is spawned then. Loads from an open bundle complete at once on both hosts (the web host fetches the bundle's files before the engine starts); only og.load.bundle of another bundle can be pending, and it completes at a tick boundary.

functions.name: bundle
functions.doc: Open another cooked bundle (the game's own `cooked` is open before the first tick). Its loads read through it once it is ready.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The cooked directory, relative to the project (or the page), such as `dlc/cooked`.

functions.returnsDoc: The bundle's handle: pending until its manifest is read, then ready or failed.

functions.name: bundleInfo
functions.doc: What an open bundle holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: asset
params.doc: A bundle handle; the game's own bundle is og.load.bundle's first answer, also given by `defaultBundle`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-bundle asset.

functions.name: defaultBundle
functions.doc: The game's own bundle, opened before the first tick from `cooked/`.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused when cooked/ was missing or unreadable (run og cook); the reason names the path.

functions.name: gltf
functions.doc: Load a cooked glTF (.gltf or .glb), as three.js GLTFLoader.load: its meshes, materials and textures join the renderer once.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The handle, or why it was refused (an uncooked path, a cook stamp mismatch, no open bundle).

functions.name: scene
functions.doc: Load a cooked scene (.ogt). world.instantiate spawns its entities: depth first, parents before children, each component table matched to a registered component by its reflected name (`Transform` is og.Transform) and migrated field by field; a field the scene lacks keeps its default, one the component lacks is dropped with a warning.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

params.name: path
params.doc: The scene's asset id, such as `scenes/main.ogt`.

functions.name: font
functions.doc: Load a cooked MSDF font for og.render.text.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

params.name: path
params.doc: The font's asset id, such as `fonts/NotoSansSC-Regular-subset.ttf`.

functions.name: fontInfo
functions.doc: A loaded font's metrics.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the font.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: sound
functions.doc: Load a cooked sound for the audio module.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

params.name: path
params.doc: The sound's asset id, such as `audio/blip.wav`.

functions.name: texture
functions.doc: Load a cooked texture for og.render.sprite and og.ui.image, as three.js TextureLoader.load.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose renderer owns the texture.

params.name: path
params.doc: The texture's asset id, such as `textures/stone.png`.

functions.name: soundInfo
functions.doc: A loaded sound's format and length.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the sound.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead sound.

functions.name: status
functions.doc: Where a load is.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.name: error
functions.doc: Why a load failed.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: The reason, naming the fix; null unless the load failed.

functions.name: gltfInfo
functions.doc: What a ready glTF holds.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world that owns the asset.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a pending, failed or non-glTF asset.

x-og-modules.name: physics
x-og-modules.doc:
Rigid bodies over rapier (rapier3d in the 3D profile, rapier2d in 2D, both with enhanced determinism): game code owns the components, the engine's og.physics system steps them after the game's systems and writes the dynamic bodies back.
The profile is the project's (`profile "2d"` or `"3d"` in project.ogt). In 2D, bodies move in the xy plane and rotate about z; a transform keeps its z. A collider without a RigidBody is static at its transform.
The rapier world persists between ticks and is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover the whole simulation. Events sent in tick N are read in tick N + 1.

consts.name: BODY_DYNAMIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: moved by the solver; its Transform and Velocity are written back every tick.

consts.name: BODY_STATIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: never moves; collides with dynamic bodies.

consts.name: BODY_KINEMATIC
consts.doc: RigidBody.kind: moved by game code through its Transform; its Velocity, if any, is how fast it pushes.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along x.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along y.

consts.name: LOCK_TRANSLATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no translation along z.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_X
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about x.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Y
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about y.

consts.name: LOCK_ROTATION_Z
consts.doc: RigidBody.lock bit: no rotation about z (the 2D profile's only rotation).

consts.name: SHAPE_BOX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a box of `size` (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_SPHERE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a sphere of `radius` (a circle in 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_CAPSULE
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a capsule along y of `radius`, with `height` between the cap centres (both profiles).

consts.name: SHAPE_CYLINDER
consts.doc: Collider.shape: a cylinder along y of `radius` and `height` (3D only).

consts.name: SHAPE_CONVEX
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the convex hull of the vertices of `mesh` (3D), or of their xy (a convex polygon, 2D).

consts.name: SHAPE_TRIMESH
consts.doc: Collider.shape: the triangles of `mesh` (3D only; for static and kinematic bodies).

consts.name: PROFILE_2D
consts.doc: Physics.profile: rapier2d, bodies in the xy plane rotating about z.

consts.name: PROFILE_3D
consts.doc: Physics.profile: rapier3d.

functions.name: raycast
functions.doc: The nearest collider along a ray. Inside a system it sees the colliders as they were at the start of the tick (og.physics.queries records them before the game's systems); between ticks, as the world holds them.
functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null when nothing is hit; refused for a zero direction.

functions.name: shapeCast
functions.doc: The first collider a shape meets when swept along a direction; the same view of the colliders as raycast.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its sweep and the filter.

functions.returnsDoc: The hit, or null; refused for a zero direction or an unknown mesh.

functions.name: overlap
functions.doc: Every collider overlapping a shape, sorted by entity id; the same view of the colliders as raycast.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The shape, its placement and the filter.

functions.name: setMesh
functions.doc: Register (or replace) the geometry a convex or triangle-mesh Collider names by its mesh handle. Loaded glTF geometries are registered under their own handles already; meshes are assets, not world state.

params.name: mesh
params.doc: The handle colliders name in Collider.mesh.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for an empty, non-finite or out-of-range mesh.

x-og-modules.name: audio
x-og-modules.doc:
Sound: inside the tick, the engine's og.audio system (after the game's systems and physics) turns AudioSource changes into a deterministic, time-stamped command stream; outside the tick the host's mixer renders it (an AudioWorklet on the web, the output device, a capture or a null sink natively).
The stream, not the PCM, is world state: snapshots, restore and the world hash cover it, and nothing a sink does reaches the world. Load sounds with og.load.sound; inserting a source plays it, setting `playing` false stops it, and a one-shot sets `playing` back to false when it ends.
Spatial gain and pan are computed in the tick from the source's og.Transform relative to the first AudioListener (three.js convention: the listener looks down -Z, +X is right; with none, the origin looking down -Z).

consts.name: SOUND_FINISHED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: a one-shot played to its end.

consts.name: SOUND_STOPPED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: `playing` was set to false.

consts.name: SOUND_REMOVED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: the AudioSource was removed from a living entity.

consts.name: SOUND_REPLACED
consts.doc: SoundEnded.reason: `sound` changed while it played.

x-og-modules.name: ui
x-og-modules.doc:
The engine's UI: an immediate-mode toolkit. Systems describe the tree every tick with these calls; the engine lays it out Clay-style, themes it with the platform's design tokens, draws it over the frame and answers the probe (dump_ui, touch_move_to, move_to_text) from it.
The engine opens the frame before the game's systems (from og.Input and the play surface) and closes it after them, so calls belong inside systems; outside one they do nothing and log a warning. Interaction is decided against the previous tick's rectangles, which are also what the probe resolves, so a scripted touch_move_to and a click agree; response edges (clicked, changed, submitted) last one tick.
Lengths are CSS pixels of the play surface (origin top left, y down), the unit of og.Input and the probe. Ids: an element's id is unique among its siblings (`idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`); a path `Inventory/Slot#3` names it after its nearest ancestors. The UI state (hover, press, focus, caret, scroll) is world state: snapshots and the world hash carry it.

functions.name: configure
functions.doc: Set the scheme, the density and the fonts, typically in GameDesc.start. Takes effect from the next tick.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose UI is configured.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a dead font.

functions.name: viewport
functions.doc: This tick's play surface: the render target's size in CSS pixels, its DPR and safe area, as the host reports them.

functions.name: theme
functions.doc: The design tokens the UI draws with.

functions.name: open
functions.doc: Open a container; the calls until its close() build its children.

params.name: id
params.doc: Its id, unique among its siblings.

functions.name: openPanel
functions.doc: Open a card, closed by close(): og.ui.panel without the callback.

functions.name: openScroll
functions.doc: Open a vertical scroll container, closed by close(): og.ui.scroll without the callback.

functions.name: close
functions.doc: Close the open container.
functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive container; the zero response otherwise.

functions.name: row
functions.doc: A row built by `build`: open(id, {...desc, direction: row}), build(), close().

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its layout and look; direction is row.

functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive row.

functions.name: column
functions.doc: A column built by `build`: open(id, {...desc, direction: column}), build(), close().

params.name: desc
params.doc: Its layout and look; direction is column.

functions.returnsDoc: Its response, for an interactive column.

functions.name: panel
functions.doc: A card built by `build`: openPanel(id, desc), build(), close().

functions.name: scroll
functions.doc: A vertical scroll container built by `build`: openScroll(id, desc), build(), close().

functions.name: label
functions.doc: MSDF text that wraps at its width (word breaks, any CJK character, long words between characters) unless nowrap. The probe reads its text.

params.name: desc
params.doc: Type step, ink, alignment, wrapping, width and font.

functions.name: button
functions.doc: A capsule button with a label; `clicked` is a press and a release inside it. The probe reads its label.

functions.name: image
functions.doc: A texture region, or a solid rectangle.

functions.name: progress
functions.doc: A capsule track filled to a fraction.

params.name: value
params.doc: How full it is, from 0 to 1.

functions.name: slider
functions.doc: A track with a fill and a thumb: a press anywhere on it sets the value and dragging follows. Pass back the value it answers next tick.

functions.name: toggle
functions.doc: A switch with a label; a click flips it. Pass back the state it answers next tick. The probe reads its label.

functions.name: textField
functions.doc: One line of text: a press focuses it with the caret at the press, typed text inserts at the caret, Backspace, Delete, arrows, Home and End edit, Enter submits and leaves, Escape leaves. Pass back the text it answers next tick. The probe reads its text, or the placeholder while empty.

functions.name: tooltip
functions.doc: A tooltip for the element just built: shown below it (above without room) once the pointer has rested on it for the slow motion duration, drawn over everything. The probe reads its text.

functions.name: idi
functions.doc: The id of the index-th of several siblings of one name: `idi("Slot", 3)` is `Slot#3`.

callbacks.name: UiBuild
callbacks.doc: Builds a container's children: ui calls made inside it nest under the container.

x-og-modules.name: systems
x-og-modules.doc: Systems the engine ships as TypeScript: game-level code, listed explicitly in GameDesc.systems like the game's own, so the schedule (and dump_world) shows them and nothing runs that the game did not ask for.

values.name: cameras
values.doc: The camera controllers, in this order: og.orbitCamera (og.OrbitCamera), og.followCamera (og.FollowCamera) and og.follow2D (og.Follow2D). Each moves og.Camera only while an entity carries its component. List them before the game's systems that read og.Camera: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`.

x-og-modules.name: commands
x-og-modules.doc:
The command channel: actions scheduled on simulation time, from `og run --commands "t:action[:args];..."` or the probe's commands().
Core actions ship with the engine; a module or a game registers more. Unknown actions warn and continue. Not in publish builds.

functions.name: register
functions.doc: Register an action into the command channel. GameDesc.commands does this for a game's own actions.

params.name: name
params.doc: The action name, snake_case, such as `spawn_wave`.

functions.returnsDoc: Refused for a name a core action or another registration already uses.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: Parse a script without scheduling it.
functions.returnsDoc: The steps, or the first malformed step.

functions.name: help
functions.doc: Every action the channel knows: core actions in CoreAction order, then registered ones by name.

params.name: world
params.doc: The world whose channel is asked.

functions.name: schedule
functions.doc: Schedule a script on simulation time, from the current tick.
functions.returnsDoc: The report, or the first malformed step.

callbacks.name: CommandHandler
callbacks.doc: A registered action. It runs at the start of the tick it was scheduled for.

params.name: args
params.doc: The `:`-separated arguments after the action name.

x-og-modules.name: probe
x-og-modules.doc:
The probe: RuntimeProbe protocol 5 (origin/packages/contracts/src/probe.ts) served natively, plus the engine's wire members.
In a page it is published on globalThis.__runtime_probe__; on native, `og` serves it as JSON-RPC 2.0 over a loopback WebSocket at /probe.
A refusal is false or null exactly as protocol 5; a JSON-RPC error is only for a malformed call or an unknown method.
Probe entity ids are entity names; an unnamed entity is `#<index>.<generation>`.

consts.name: PROBE_GLOBAL
consts.doc: The global the page publishes the probe on.

consts.name: PROBE_VERSION
consts.doc: The RuntimeProbe contract revision both sides speak.

consts.name: PROBE_WIRE_VERSION
consts.doc: The wire revision hello reports.

consts.name: REPLAY_SEED_PARAM
consts.doc: The page query parameter that starts a deterministic replay from a uint32 seed.

consts.name: PLAYTEST_MAX_TICKS
consts.doc: The longest playtest one request may advance, in fixed steps.

consts.name: PROBE_PROGRAM_MAX_OPERATIONS
consts.doc: The most operations one probe program may carry.

interfaces.name: RuntimeProbe
interfaces.doc: RuntimeProbe protocol 5, member for member. Every member answers synchronously with JSON-serialisable values.

members.name: version
members.doc: PROBE_VERSION.

members.name: tick
members.doc: Fixed steps the world has taken since load.

members.name: state
members.doc: A JSON snapshot: the fixed timings head, then the game's own facts.

members.name: advance
members.doc: Take whole fixed steps regardless of the wall clock.
members.returnsDoc: The tick after the steps.

members.name: pause
members.doc: Hold the wall-clock loop; advance still steps.

members.name: resume
members.doc: Release the wall-clock loop.

members.name: input
members.doc: One event through the input layer's own path.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: accepted
members.doc: Page events (keyboard, pointer, wheel) the input layer accepted since load.

members.name: pick
members.doc: What is under a point of the play surface.
members.returnsDoc: Null when nothing is under the point.

members.name: entity
members.doc: One entity's published parameters: its tunable fields as `Component.field` keys.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: bounds
members.doc: The ranges of one entity's tunable fields, from the schema.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: patch
members.doc: Move one tunable field for this run only; it applies within one frame. The probe never writes project files.
members.returnsDoc: False is a refusal.

members.name: run
members.doc: Run a program of the members above in order, stopping at the first refusal.

interfaces.name: EngineProbe
interfaces.doc: The engine's probe: protocol 5 plus the wire members of the loopback WebSocket and the in-page request ring.

members.name: hello
members.doc: Who is speaking: protocol, wire, engine version, tick rate, renderer tier, build.

members.name: capture
members.doc:
The frame of the current tick, rendered offscreen and read back as a PNG.
Size rule: width and height are both 0 (or absent), which is the render target's size, or both 1 to 4096, which renders that size with the same camera (the aspect follows the requested size); one zero and one not is a malformed call.
On the web the readback is asynchronous: through the request ring the answer arrives when the copy completes; a synchronous in-page call answers null on the first tick and the frame from then on (a capture is requested on tick N and answered on N + 1).

params.name: width
params.doc: Width in pixels; 0 is the render target's.

params.name: height
params.doc: Height in pixels; 0 is the render target's.

members.returnsDoc: Null without a renderer.

members.name: sweep
members.doc: A filmstrip over one tunable: per value, restore, patch, advance, capture.

params.name: desc
params.doc: The parameter, values, steps and size.

members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity or parameter, or without a renderer.

members.name: reload
members.doc: Hot reload: snapshot, swap the game bundle, re-register components by name, restore.
members.returnsDoc: Null when the new bundle fails to load; the old one keeps running.

members.name: snapshot
members.doc: Snapshot the whole world in the running process.

members.name: restore
members.doc: Restore a snapshot taken by this process.
members.returnsDoc: False for an unknown id.

members.name: dump
members.doc: A world, entity or UI dump, as the command channel's dump actions write.
members.returnsDoc: Null for an unknown entity.

members.name: commands
members.doc: Schedule a command script on simulation time, as `og run --commands`.
members.returnsDoc: Null for a malformed script.

Vector3.description: A 3D vector, as three.js Vector3. The engine is right-handed with +Y up, as three.js.

Quaternion.description: A unit quaternion rotation, as three.js Quaternion. The zero value is the identity.

Matrix4.description: A 4x4 matrix, as three.js Matrix4: sixteen elements in column-major order. The zero value is the identity.

elements.description: The elements, column-major, as three.js Matrix4.elements.

Color.description: A linear RGB colour, as three.js Color with colour management on. Components are usually between 0 and 1; above 1 is HDR.

direction.description: The unit direction the ray points in.

FieldOptions.description: Metadata of one field. Ranges and units are what Tune and the probe's bounds show; nothing clamps writes.

unit.description: A unit name from the API's unit table, or empty.

label.description: The person-facing name; empty uses the field name.

doc.description: One sentence on what the field means.

tunable.description: Publish the field to Tune and to the probe's bounds and patch.

Entity.description:
An entity: an index and a generation. The value is index + generation * 2^32, with the generation below 2^21, so it stays an exact JavaScript number.
Generations start at 1, so 0 is never a live entity.

SpawnDesc.description: How to spawn an entity. `{}` spawns an unnamed entity at the origin with a Transform.

name.description: A unique name; the probe and the command channel address the entity by it. Empty leaves it unnamed.

parent.description: The parent entity; the new entity's Transform is then relative to it.

bare.description: Spawn without a Transform: a pure data entity.

without.description: Components an entity must not have.

SystemDesc.description: A system's declared access and order.

reads.description: Components, resources and events the system reads (world.events). Components here also shape its query.

writes.description: Components, resources and events the system writes (world.emit). Components here also shape its query.

without.description: Components a matched entity must not have.

after.description: Names of systems that must run before this one.

before.description: Names of systems that must run after this one.

GameDesc.description: A game: its tick, scenes, systems and commands.

seed.description: The project seed every Rng stream derives from. A replay overrides it.

scenes.description: Scene names to `.ogt` paths, as `{ main: "scenes/main.ogt" }`.

systems.description: The systems, in declaration order before `after`/`before` constraints apply.

resources.description: The game's own resources, created at their defaults.

commands.description: Game actions registered into the command channel, by action name.

maxCatchUp.description: The most ticks one frame may run to catch up with the clock; the accumulator drops the rest.

facts.description: The game's own facts for the probe's state().

start.description: Called once before the first tick, after the first scene spawned.

render.description: How the renderer is created: antialiasing and shadow map size. Read once, when the host attaches the renderer.

Transform.description: Where an entity is, relative to its parent (or the world).

Parent.description: The entity this one's Transform is relative to. Set by SpawnDesc.parent.

MatrixWorld.description: The world matrix the engine composes after the systems run, as three.js Object3D.matrixWorld.

Time.description: The fixed tick's clock. Every value is a function of the tick count, so a replay sees the same numbers.

dt.description: The length of one tick: 1 / rate.

elapsed.description: Simulation time since load: tick * dt.

Rng.description: The world's main random stream, seeded from GameDesc.seed (or the replay seed). Its state is part of every snapshot.

seed.description: The seed the stream started from.

state.description: The generator state; snapshot and restore carry it.

KeyAction.description: What an injected key event does.

x-og-variants.press: Down, then up on the next tick.

PointerAction.description: What an injected pointer event does.

x-og-variants.click: Down, then up on the next tick, at the point.

PointerButton.description: A physical pointer button; `none` is a hover move.

x-og-variants.left: The primary button, or a touch.

Modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during a key event.

platform.description: Command on macOS, the Windows key on Windows.

KeyInput.description: A key event. `key` names the physical key as KeyboardEvent.code does: ArrowRight, Space, KeyA.

PointerInput.description: A pointer event at a point in CSS pixels of the play surface.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

WheelInput.description: A wheel or trackpad scroll at a point.

InjectedInput.description: One input event in the game's own vocabulary, as the probe's input() and playtest scripts carry it.

button.description: The button; `none` for a hover move.

Input.description:
The input state at the start of this tick (og-input's og.Input, version 2). Edges (pressed, released) last exactly one tick; read the state through the methods.
Key sets are 128 bits over og-input's KEY_CODES (KeyboardEvent.code names): code i is bit i % 32 of word i / 32. Button masks: left 1, middle 2, right 4.

pointerInside.description: Whether a pointer event has placed the pointer over the play surface.

buttons.description: Held pointer buttons, as a mask.

buttonsPressed.description: Buttons that went down this tick.

buttonsReleased.description: Buttons that went up this tick.

buttonsReleaseNext.description: Buttons a click releases at the end of the next tick.

keys0.description: Held keys, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

keys1.description: Held keys, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

keys2.description: Held keys, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

keys3.description: Held keys, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

pressed0.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

pressed1.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

pressed2.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

pressed3.description: Keys that went down this tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

released0.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

released1.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

released2.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

released3.description: Keys that went up this tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext0.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 0: codes 0 to 31 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext1.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 1: codes 32 to 63 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext2.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 2: codes 64 to 95 of KEY_CODES.

releaseNext3.description: Keys a press releases at the end of the next tick, word 3: codes 96 to 127 of KEY_CODES.

KeyDown.description: A key went down (a down for a held key is a repeat and sets no edge). Input events are sent between ticks and read by the next tick's systems.

Camera.description: The camera the frame is rendered from. Rendering reads it after the tick; it never feeds back into the simulation.

quaternion.description: Its rotation; the camera looks down its local -Z.

fov.description: The vertical field of view of the perspective projection.

zoom.description: The zoom factor, as three.js Camera.zoom.

orthographic.description: Use an orthographic projection (the 2D profile) instead of a perspective one.

height.description: The visible world height of the orthographic projection.

background.description: The clear colour, as three.js Scene.background. The default is the brand ink #14161b in linear RGB.

exposure.description: Exposure before tone mapping, as three.js toneMappingExposure.

OrbitCamera.description:
Orbits og.Camera around the entity carrying it, as three.js OrbitControls: a left-button drag on the play surface turns it, the wheel zooms, autoRotate turns it on its own.
Camera controllers are game-level systems the engine ships in TypeScript (og.systems.cameras); list them in GameDesc.systems: `systems: [...og.systems.cameras, ...yours]`. The first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.
The camera sits `distance` from the orbited point (the entity's position plus `target`) in the direction given by `azimuth` about +Y and `polar` from +Y, and looks at the point. Every angle is computed with deterministic arithmetic, so a replay moves the camera identically on every host.

target.description: The orbited point, relative to the entity's position.

distance.description: How far the camera is from the orbited point, as three.js OrbitControls' distance.

minDistance.description: The closest the wheel zooms in, as three.js OrbitControls.minDistance.

maxDistance.description: The farthest the wheel zooms out, as three.js OrbitControls.maxDistance.

azimuth.description: The horizontal angle about +Y; 0 puts the camera on the +Z side of the point.

polar.description: The angle from +Y: near 0 looks straight down, half pi is level with the point.

minPolarAngle.description: The smallest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.minPolarAngle.

maxPolarAngle.description: The largest polar angle a drag reaches, as three.js OrbitControls.maxPolarAngle.

rotateSpeed.description: Drag sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.rotateSpeed: at 1, dragging the play surface's height turns a full circle.

zoomSpeed.description: Wheel sensitivity, as three.js OrbitControls.zoomSpeed: at 1, 100 CSS pixels of wheel change the distance by a tenth.

autoRotate.description: Turn about the point on its own while not dragged, as three.js OrbitControls.autoRotate.

enabled.description: Read the pointer and the wheel; false keeps only autoRotate and the fields' own values.

dragging.description: Controller state: a left-button drag that started on the play surface is in progress.

pointer.description: Controller state: where the pointer was on the previous tick of a drag.

FollowCamera.description: Chases the entity carrying it with og.Camera: a third-person 3D view that eases towards a point offset from the entity and looks at it. Driven by og.systems.cameras; the first entity carrying one, in query order, drives the camera.

offset.description: Where the camera sits relative to the entity: in the entity's own axes with followRotation, else in world axes.

lookOffset.description: The point the camera looks at, relative to the entity's position.

followRotation.description: Turn the offset with the entity's rotation, so the camera stays behind it.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up with a moved entity; 0 snaps it there every tick.

Follow2D.description: Keeps og.Camera on the entity carrying it in the xy plane, for 2D games: the camera moves only when the entity leaves the dead zone, eases by smoothTime and, with clamp, stays inside the bounds. The camera keeps its z, rotation and projection. Driven by og.systems.cameras.

offset.description: Where the camera centre sits relative to the entity.

deadZone.description: Half the width and height of the box around the camera centre inside which the entity moves without moving the camera.

smoothTime.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to catch up; 0 snaps it every tick.

clamp.description: Keep the camera centre between boundsMin and boundsMax.

boundsMin.description: The smallest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

boundsMax.description: The largest x and y the camera centre takes with clamp.

Geometry.description: Vertex and index data, as three.js BufferGeometry. Comes from a loaded glTF.

Side.description: Which faces are drawn, as three.js FrontSide, BackSide and DoubleSide.

RenderTier.description: The backend the renderer runs on; the probe's hello reports it.

x-og-variants.webgpu: WebGPU in a browser: the full feature set.
x-og-variants.webgl2: The WebGL2 fallback: no compute, CPU culling and particles, tiled lights.
x-og-variants.vulkan: Native Vulkan, on lavapipe or a GPU.
x-og-variants.none: No renderer: frames are not produced and capture refuses.

Antialias.description: Antialiasing, as og-render's Antialias. RenderCapabilities.antialias reports what the device resolved.

x-og-variants.tier: The tier's method: TAA on the full tier (WebGPU, Metal, Vulkan), 4x MSAA on WebGL2.
x-og-variants.msaa4: 4x MSAA on any tier: sharp sprites and text, no temporal blur; off where the HDR format cannot be multisampled.
x-og-variants.taa: Temporal antialiasing on any tier: a sub-pixel jitter per frame and a reprojected history; converges over about eight frames.

RenderOptions.description: How the renderer is created for a game (GameDesc.render). The host reads it once, when it attaches the renderer.

shadowMapSize.description: The side of each of the directional light's three cascade maps, in texels; smaller saves memory on phones (three 2048 maps are 64 MB).

StandardMaterialDesc.description:
A physically based metallic-roughness material with three.js MeshStandardMaterial parameter names.
Mapping to the renderer (og-render Material): color and opacity are the base colour and its alpha; map the base colour texture; metalness and roughness the factors; metalnessMap and roughnessMap are one glTF metallic-roughness texture (blue metal, green rough), so give both the same texture; normalMap the normal texture; emissive times emissiveIntensity the emitted colour, emissiveMap its texture; alphaTest above 0 is alpha masking with that cutoff.
Accepted and kept but not drawn yet: aoMap, transparent (blending), side (meshes draw front faces), flatShading and envMapIntensity; the renderer's own phase-2 list owns them.

metalnessMap.description: Metalness from the texture's blue channel.

roughnessMap.description: Roughness from the texture's green channel.

aoMap.description: Ambient occlusion from the texture's red channel.

emissiveIntensity.description: A multiplier on the emitted colour.

opacity.description: The opacity; below 1 only with transparent.

transparent.description: Blend instead of writing opaque pixels.

alphaTest.description: Discard pixels whose alpha is below this.

Mesh.description:
Draws a geometry with a material at the entity's MatrixWorld, as a three.js Mesh.
The material is a handle from og.render.standardMaterial or from a loaded glTF (GltfInfo.materials); its StandardMaterialDesc maps to the renderer as that struct's docs say.

DirectionalLight.description:
The sun, as three.js DirectionalLight: parallel light along the entity's local -Z (aim it with transform.lookAt, as a camera). The first one found is drawn, with three shadow cascades.
Without one, the renderer's default sun (from above and to the side, intensity 3) lights the scene.

intensity.description: The radiance multiplier, as three.js DirectionalLight.intensity.

castShadow.description: Cast shadows through three cascades, as three.js Light.castShadow.

shadowDistance.description: How far from the camera shadows reach; they fade over the last tenth. Smaller is sharper.

PointLight.description:
A light shining in every direction from the entity's position, as three.js PointLight. Its radiance at distance d is color * intensity / d^2, faded smoothly to zero at distance.
Up to MAX_LIGHTS point and spot lights are drawn per frame (the rest are counted, not drawn); the first two with castShadow get cube shadows.

distance.description: Where the light reaches zero, as three.js PointLight.distance (never infinite here).

SpotLight.description: A cone of light along the entity's local -Z, as three.js SpotLight.

intensity.description: The radiance at one metre on the axis.

angle.description: The half-angle of the outer cone, as three.js SpotLight.angle.

penumbra.description: The fraction of the cone over which the light fades out, as three.js SpotLight.penumbra.

RenderSettings.description: The frame's look after lighting: environment light, sky, bloom, exposure metering and tone mapping. Read after each tick; it never feeds back into the simulation. Camera.exposure is the manual exposure.

environmentIntensity.description: The strength of the image-based ambient light from the procedural sky.

sky.description: Draw the procedural sky behind the scene instead of Camera.background.

bloom.description: Light above the threshold bleeds into its surroundings.

bloomThreshold.description: Brightness after exposure where bloom starts; 1 is display white.

bloomKnee.description: Softens the threshold over threshold plus or minus knee; 0 is a hard cut.

bloomIntensity.description: How much of the blurred light is added back.

autoExposure.description: Meter every frame to middle grey (deterministic: the current frame only), then apply Camera.exposure as compensation.

toneMapped.description: ACES tone mapping; false clamps, so 2D colours come out exactly as authored at exposure 1.

TextDesc.description: A line or block of MSDF text in the world's xy plane facing +z, drawn this frame only (immediate mode: submit it every tick it should show).

font.description: The font from og.load.font; null draws nothing.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

position.description: The baseline origin of the first line.

size.description: The em size in world units.

layer.description: Draw order among sprites and text; higher draws on top.

align.description: How each line sits on `position`: start puts its left end there, center its middle, end its right end.

TextMeasureDesc.description: Text to measure with og.render.measureText, laid out as og.render.text lays it out.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

size.description: The em size in world units.

TextMetrics.description: The extent of a laid-out text, in world units.

height.description: Lines times the font's line height.

SpriteDesc.description: A textured or solid quad in the world's xy plane facing +z, drawn this frame only (immediate mode, as og.render.text): submit it every tick it should show. Sprites and text are sorted by layer and drawn over the 3D scene.

texture.description: The texture from og.load.texture; null draws a solid quad of the colour.

anchor.description: The point of the quad at `position`, as a fraction of its size from the bottom-left corner: (0.5, 0.5) is the centre.

color.description: A linear colour multiplied with the texture.

uv.description: The texture region drawn, [u0, v0, u1, v1] with v down; null is the whole texture (a sheet's frame for animation).

layer.description: Draw order among sprites and text; higher draws on top.

BoxGeometryDesc.description: A box centred at the origin, as three.js BoxGeometry(width, height, depth).

PlaneGeometryDesc.description: A rectangle in the xy plane facing +z, centred at the origin, as three.js PlaneGeometry(width, height); turn it -pi/2 about x for a floor.

SphereGeometryDesc.description: A UV sphere centred at the origin, as three.js SphereGeometry(radius, widthSegments, heightSegments).

RenderCapabilities.description: What the renderer can do on this device. Backend limits are reported here, never by missing members.

compute.description: Whether compute passes run (GPU culling, GPU particles).

antialias.description: The antialiasing the device resolved RenderOptions.antialias to.

maxLights.description: How many point and spot lights one frame draws.

maxShadowedLights.description: How many point and spot lights may cast shadows.

width.description: The render target width in device pixels.

height.description: The render target height in device pixels.

Asset.description: A loaded bundle, scene or glTF asset.

Font.description: A cooked MSDF font: its glyph table and one or more atlas pages.

Sound.description: A cooked sound: QOA-encoded PCM the audio module plays.

GltfDesc.description: How to load a glTF, as three.js GLTFLoader options where they apply.

castShadow.description: Set Mesh.castShadow on every mesh instantiated from it.

receiveShadow.description: Set Mesh.receiveShadow on every mesh instantiated from it.

geometries.description: Its geometries, in glTF mesh-primitive order.

materials.description: Its materials, in glTF order, then the default material.

animations.description: Its animation clip names (the cook counts clips and does not cook them yet, so this is empty).

path.description: The cooked directory it was opened from.

FontInfo.description: A loaded font's metrics, in em units unless stated.

pages.description: Atlas pages; the renderer draws one page per pass with one shared layout.

pxRange.description: The distance range in atlas pixels.

lineHeight.description: Ascender minus descender plus the line gap.

Model.description: Draws a loaded glTF's default scene at the entity's world transform: every mesh node with its glTF material. Scene entities with a `model` line get one; world.instantiate of a glTF asset spawns one.

path.description: The path it was loaded from.
The path it was loaded from.

RigidBody.description:
A body the physics step simulates. It needs an og.Transform and usually has an og.Collider; a dynamic body without an og.Velocity gets one.
Changing a RigidBody, a Collider or Transform.scale rebuilds the body (it loses its contacts' warm starts); a Transform or Velocity that game code changed moves it (a teleport).

kind.description: BODY_DYNAMIC (0, simulated and written back), BODY_STATIC (1, never moves) or BODY_KINEMATIC (2, moved by game code through its Transform).

mass.description: Mass; 0 derives it from the collider's density and volume.

linearDamping.description: How fast linear velocity decays (0: none).

angularDamping.description: How fast angular velocity decays (0: none).

gravityScale.description: Multiplies Physics.gravity for this body: 0 floats, 1 is normal.

lock.description: Locked axes, a sum of the LOCK_* bits: 1, 2, 4 no translation along x, y, z; 8, 16, 32 no rotation about x, y, z (2D uses 1, 2 and 32).

ccd.description: 1 enables continuous collision detection, for fast small bodies that must not tunnel; 0 off.

Collider.description: The shape an entity collides with, attached to its RigidBody (or, without one, a static collider at its Transform). Sizes are scaled by og.Transform.scale.

shape.description: One of the SHAPE_* codes: 0 box, 1 sphere (a circle in 2D), 2 capsule, 3 cylinder (3D), 4 convex hull of `mesh` (a polygon in 2D), 5 triangle mesh of `mesh` (3D).

size.description: Full extents of a box, as three.js BoxGeometry(width, height, depth).

radius.description: Radius of a sphere, circle, capsule or cylinder.

height.description: A capsule's distance between its cap centres (three.js CapsuleGeometry length); a cylinder's height.

mesh.description: The geometry whose vertices a convex or triangle-mesh shape uses: a loaded glTF's geometry (registered automatically) or one given to og.physics.setMesh.

offset.description: Position of the shape relative to the entity.

rotation.description: Rotation of the shape relative to the entity.

friction.description: Coulomb friction (0 is ice, 1 rubber); a pair uses the mean of both colliders.

restitution.description: Bounciness (0 no bounce, 1 elastic); a pair uses the mean of both colliders.

sensor.description: 1 makes this a sensor: it reports SensorEntered and SensorExited and pushes nothing; 0 a solid.

layers.description: The collision layers this collider is on, as bits.

mask.description: The layers it collides with, as bits. Two colliders interact when each one's layers meet the other's mask.

Velocity.description: Linear and angular velocity. Written for dynamic bodies every tick (added to them by the step when missing), read for kinematic ones; set it to launch or stop a body.

linear.description: The linear velocity (2D uses x and y).

angular.description: The angular velocity about each axis (2D uses z).

Physics.description: The physics settings of the world. The profile is the project's; the same components serve both profiles.

profile.description: PROFILE_2D (2: rapier2d, the xy plane, rotation about z) or PROFILE_3D (3: rapier3d), from project.ogt.

gravity.description: The acceleration of every dynamic body, times its gravityScale; 2D uses x and y.

substeps.description: Physics steps per tick, each of dt / substeps: more is stiffer stacks and less tunnelling, at more cost.

restSpeed.description: A dynamic body touching something, supported with at most 2 mm of overlap and slower than this before and after a step, keeps its pose and loses its residual velocity (the same number in m/s and rad/s); 0 disables it.

CollisionStarted.description: Two solid colliders started touching during the tick.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

point.description: The deepest contact point in world space (z is 0 in 2D).

normal.description: The contact normal, from a towards b.

CollisionEnded.description: Two solid colliders stopped touching, or one of them went away.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

SensorEntered.description: A collider started overlapping a sensor.

sensor.description: The entity whose collider is the sensor.

SensorExited.description: A collider stopped overlapping a sensor, or one of them went away.

sensor.description: The entity whose collider is the sensor.

Contact.description: One pair in contact at the end of a step, sent every tick for every touching pair: how a game asks what is touching what right now.

a.description: The entity with the lower id.

b.description: The entity with the higher id.

sensor.description: 0 for two solids; an overlap with a sensor otherwise: 1 a is the sensor, 2 b is, 3 both are.

QueryFilter.description: Which colliders a scene query considers. The zero value considers every solid collider on every layer.

mask.description: Layers to consider: a collider counts when its layers meet this; 0 means every layer.

exclude.description: An entity to ignore, such as the caster itself.

direction.description: Where it points; it need not be normalised and must not be zero (in 2D, not zero in xy).

maxDistance.description: How far it reaches; 0 is unbounded.

RaycastHit.description: The nearest collider a ray meets.

distance.description: From the origin along the normalised direction.

point.description: Where the ray meets the collider.

AudioSource.description:
A sound an entity plays. Level-triggered: while `playing` is true it plays (inserting a source plays it), setting it false stops it, and a one-shot that reaches its end sets it back to false and sends og.SoundEnded.
A one-shot of F frames at rate R and pitch p started in tick S ends in tick S + ceil(F * tickRate / (R * p)) - 1. A despawned entity's voice is silenced without an event.

sound.description: The sound, from og.load.sound; 0 plays nothing. A handle not yet loaded waits and starts on the first tick it is there.

pitch.description: Playback rate: 2 is an octave up and half as long.

pan.description: Stereo position of a non-spatial source, -1 left to 1 right.

loop.description: Loop between loopStart and loopEnd, seamlessly.

loopEnd.description: Where a loop wraps; 0 is the sound's end.

spatial.description: Attenuate and pan by the entity's og.Transform relative to the listener.

refDistance.description: Full volume up to this distance, as Web Audio's PannerNode.refDistance.

maxDistance.description: No quieter past this distance, as Web Audio's PannerNode.maxDistance.

rolloffFactor.description: How fast volume falls with distance, in Web Audio's inverse model: ref / (ref + rolloff * (clamp(d, ref, max) - ref)).

playing.description: Plays while true; the engine sets it false when a one-shot ends.

AudioListener.description: Where spatial sources are heard from: the entity's og.Transform, looking down its -Z with +X to the right. The first listener in query order is used.

volume.description: A gain on every spatial source this listener hears.

Audio.description: Bus volumes; master scales every bus. A change ramps over 256 frames in the mixer.

master.description: Gain of the master bus, applied to every sound.

SoundStarted.description: A source started, sent in the tick it happens (systems read it the tick after).

voice.description: The voice id in the command stream.

SoundEnded.description: A sound ended, sent in the tick it happens (systems read it the tick after).

voice.description: The voice id in the command stream.

reason.description: Why: SOUND_FINISHED (0), SOUND_STOPPED (1), SOUND_REMOVED (2) or SOUND_REPLACED (3).
